meta.description: Fail-closed baseline — the full HealthKit control universe, every read/write facet.
Least-restrictive floor — explicit consent + usage description always required for health data.
Fail-closed baseline — full location control universe; background delivery denied, precise accuracy opt-in only.
Least-restrictive floor — consent + usage description; always-authorization never granted.
Fail-closed baseline — full Core NFC control universe; tag writes hard-denied, every scan session-scoped.
Least-restrictive floor — consent + usage description; every scan session-scoped, never ambient polling.
Fail-closed baseline — full Photos control universe; limited selection + EXIF-location withholding required.
Least-restrictive floor — consent + usage description; scoped picker access preferred over full-library.
Fail-closed baseline — full HomeKit control universe; state-changing control requires a confirmation token.
Least-restrictive floor — consent + usage description; unconfirmed home-actuation never allowed.

catalog.description: {Catalog} Object Block — the Control Catalog ledger, one entry per domain

policies.description: {Policies} Object Block — regulatory policy pack ledger

snapp_compliance.description: {SnappCompliance} Object Block — what a Snapp declares it exercises and handles

id.description: OPTIONAL pack id. On disk the profile and domain ARE the path, and in an emitted bundle the pack's declaration name is its key — so an id is only useful when a reader needs a stable handle that is neither.

meta.description: Posture + review provenance. NESTED rather than flattened so the typed source mirrors the published pack's `[meta]` / `[meta.legal_review]` tables: a flat `legal_review_status` cannot round-trip to `[meta.legal_review] status` without a projection rule, and a projection rule is a place for the two to disagree.

subject.description: Per-subject required-control table. SINGULAR to match the published pack schema, whose `subject` is an object of `control_list` — which is exactly what the keyword form already emits. It was `subjects` until 2026-10-16, and that one letter was the whole reason a consumer had to project the emitted bundle before anything could validate it.

legally_required.description: Controls required under minimal strictness / when no subject row matches. WRAPPED in a ControlList rather than a bare list so the emitted bytes match the published pack's `[legally_required] controls = [...]` table and validate against schema/pack.schema.json, whose `legally_required` is a `$ref` to `control_list`. A bare list emitted a bare array, and the gap between the two is what a consumer had to project around.

prohibited.description: Controls this profile FORBIDS — the data-minimization guard input: no posture may ADD a control listed here, and a resolver subtracts it from every resolved set. MUST NOT intersect legally_required (a pack that both requires and forbids a control is not satisfiable). OPTIONAL: an absent list forbids nothing, which is why it is not the same as an empty one in review.

PackMeta.description: {PackMeta} Object Block — the pack's posture and its review provenance

description.description: Human-readable pack description. Named `description` to match the published pack's `[meta] description`: this field was called `summary` here until 2026-10-15, which meant the typed source and the artifact a reviewer reads used different names for the same sentence.

legal_review.description: Who reviewed this pack and how far that review went

effective_from.description: ISO-8601 (YYYY-MM-DD) date this pack's text takes effect. A decision date before this means no in-effect pack governs.

effective_until.description: ISO-8601 (YYYY-MM-DD) date this pack's text stops being in effect. A decision date after this means no in-effect pack governs.

last_reviewed_against_guidance.description: Interpretation-currency date — when this pack was last read against case law and regulator guidance, which is NOT the same as the statute's effective date. REQUIRED by the published schema once `legal_review.status` is `approved`: an approval nobody can age is indistinguishable from one that never expires.

inherits.description: Parent profile this pack delta-inherits from, as a `/`-delimited profile tag. Declaring it does not make a resolver honour it — progressive-truncation negotiation and delta-merge are specified but unimplemented in the reference resolver, so treat this as authored-ahead.

LegalReview.description: {LegalReview} Object Block — counsel-review provenance for one pack

counsel.description: Reviewing counsel of record (\"TBD\" until assigned); REQUIRED before a real-jurisdiction pack ships

reviewed.description: ISO-8601 (YYYY-MM-DD) date the pack was last reviewed. A quoted YYYY-MM-DD literal is shape-typed `date`, not `str`. An `approved` real-jurisdiction pack must state this: an approval with no date cannot be aged, and a review nobody can age is indistinguishable from a review that never expires.

Subject.description: {Subject} Object Block — one capability facet and its required controls

key.description: Gate subject key (capability facet: read, write, control, enumerate, …)

controls.description: Required opaque control keys for this subject (the gate owns polarity)

ControlList.description: {ControlList} Object Block — a named list of control keys, as a TABLE

controls.description: Opaque control keys. EMPTY IS MEANINGFUL and is not the same as absent: an empty list under `prohibited` forbids nothing explicitly, where an absent `prohibited` was never reviewed. The resolver's reader carries a serde default for exactly this reason.

ControlCatalog.description: {ControlCatalog} Object Block — one domain's control vocabulary

domain.description: The domain this catalog declares. NESTED to mirror the published `[domain]` table rather than flattened to `domain_name`, so the typed source and the artifact a reader opens use one shape.

control.description: The control keys, as a KEYED table — `[control.<key>]` in the artifact. A list of `{key, ...}` rows would emit an array and need projecting before it matched the published document.

CatalogDomain.description: {CatalogDomain} Object Block — which domain a catalog speaks for

name.description: The domain name, which spec §2.2 makes the pack FILENAME on disk. A catalog whose name disagrees with its filename validates the wrong domain's packs while every log line names the right one.

description.description: What this domain governs, in one sentence a reviewer reads before the key list.

ControlTable.description: {ControlTable} Object Block — control keys to their definitions, keyed by the key itself

ControlDef.description: {ControlDef} Object Block — one control key: what kind of thing it is, and what it names

kind.description: The deontic kind. A PROHIBITION is subtracted from every resolved set under every posture, so it must never appear in a requirement table — a pack that both requires and forbids a control is not satisfiable. Closed because a wrong kind inverts the control's meaning rather than degrading it.

title.description: A short human-readable title. `r14n extract` emits it into generated pack templates, so an empty one ships into other people's files.

description.description: What the control names, and where its satisfier lives. OPTIONAL in shape, expected in practice — the catalog is where a reader learns what a key MEANS, since the key itself is opaque.

trigger.description: When the enforcing gate must satisfy it (e.g. `before_capture`, `before_redeem`, `always`). A facet, not a schedule: the gate owns timing.

mechanism.description: A stable name for HOW the control is discharged, for a receipt reader correlating a decision with an enforcement path.

deprecated.description: The date this key was deprecated. A control key is long-lived audit evidence (invariant 10), so a retired key is DEPRECATED rather than deleted: receipts already issued name it, and a reader of one needs it to still resolve.

superseded_by.description: What to use instead. Cross-domain successors are spelled `<domain>::<key>`, because a key is namespaced by its owning domain (spec §2) and a bare name would be ambiguous. A deprecation without this leaves the holder of an issued receipt no forward path.

frameworks.description: OPTIONAL typed links from this control to the compliance-framework EDITIONS it relates to (see the `frameworks` keyword doc). A pointer for a human reviewer, never a determination: it does not say the control is sufficient for, or satisfies, any criterion, and it is NOT LEGAL ADVICE. A resolver MUST NOT vary a decision on it. Absent means no link has been made, which is not the same as no relationship existing. ADDITIVE: a control without this prop validates exactly as before.

verified_by.description: A pointer to the external specification section that defines how this control is verified (an interoperability spec's anchor). For a human tracing a control to its defining text; never dereferenced by a resolver. Declared here because shipped catalogs use it and an undeclared prop is REFUSED by default, so without this a catalog carrying it could not be authored through the typed path.

attestation_mode.description: Which attestation mode this control requires, where a domain has more than one and they are NOT interchangeable. Open rather than closed: the shipped values are a two-member set in one domain, and closing it here would refuse a domain whose modes this vocabulary has not met. Two controls may share a mechanism and differ only here; the control KEY carries the distinction in a receipt.

subject_rights.description: Data-subject rights this control bears on (for example withdrawal). Informational: it tells a reviewer which right a control serves, and asserts nothing about whether that right applies in any jurisdiction.

legal_basis_hint.description: A HINT at the consent or processing model a control is usually associated with. The name hedges on purpose and the hedge is load-bearing: a catalog is jurisdiction-neutral and NOT LEGAL ADVICE, so this is a pointer for a human reviewer choosing which packs to author - never a determination, never evidence a basis is available, and a resolver MUST NOT vary a decision on it.

FrameworkReview.description: {FrameworkReview} Object Block — where the review of one framework link stands

status.description: Where the review stands. `draft` — being written. `requires_signoff` — awaiting a named reviewer. `approved` — a named reviewer has signed off. `approved` records that a review HAPPENED; it is not a finding that the link, or anything it names, is lawful, sufficient or current. A closed set, and NOT LegalReview's: that set also carries `not_required`, which has no meaning for a link.

counsel.description: Who reviewed, as a free-form string. Not verified here, not a legal credential (nothing checks that it names a lawyer, a firm or a person), and not an attorney-of-record claim: that contract belongs to a pack's `legal_review`, which this field neither replaces nor mirrors.

FrameworkLink.description: {FrameworkLink} Object Block — one control's link to one framework edition: HOW it relates, WHERE, and who has looked

relation.description: How the control relates to the edition. `informs` — background. `contributes` — one part of what an organization might do about a criterion. `necessary` — a reviewer has recorded that the criterion cannot be addressed without it (a recorded claim, never verified here); NOT `sufficient`. Closed, and deliberately without `satisfies`, `meets` or `complies`. `necessary` REQUIRES a `review` with status `approved` — a rule these types cannot express (see the tripwires), carried by the published catalog schema.

criteria.description: Identifiers of the edition's criteria this link bears on, spelled as the framework's publisher spells them. Optional, and an EMPTY list is refused: it reads as answered, which is worse than absent. Ships EMPTY OF REAL IDENTIFIERS until licensing is cleared; fixtures use `EXAMPLE-1`. Item atom kind and non-emptiness are NOT enforced by these types (list items do not enforce); the published catalog schema carries them.

review.description: Who has looked at this link, and where it stands. Optional in general; REQUIRED when `relation` is `necessary` (with status `approved`) and for ANY link to `hipaa_45cfr164_2013`. Neither requirement is enforced by these types.

FrameworkLinks.description: {FrameworkLinks} Object Block — OPTIONAL typed links from one control to the framework EDITIONS it relates to. A pointer for a human, never a determination: it does not say a control is sufficient for, or satisfies, any criterion, and a resolver MUST NOT vary a decision on it. NOT LEGAL ADVICE

soc2_tsc_2017.description: Link to the 2017 edition of a SOC 2 trust-services criteria set.

iso27001_2022_a1_2024.description: Link to the 2022 edition of an ISO 27001 information-security standard as amended in 2024.

hipaa_45cfr164_2013.description: Link to the 2013 edition of the HIPAA 45 CFR part 164 text. A legal-text edition (a regulation): a link to it REQUIRES a `review` block (not enforced by this type).

hecvat_4_1_6.description: Link to version 4.1.6 of the HECVAT higher-education vendor assessment.

SnappCompliance.description: {SnappCompliance} Object Block — the (domain, subject) pairs a Snapp exercises and the data classes it handles. A declaration, not a determination. NOT LEGAL ADVICE

exercises.description: The domains this Snapp exercises, as a KEYED table: domain -> the subjects of that domain it exercises. REQUIRED. At least one entry is expected (an `exercises` table with none says nothing); that is NOT enforced when this table is nested here (see the tripwire), and is left to the block's JSON schema.

data_classes.description: The data classes this Snapp handles, as SUBJECT tokens (`^[a-z][a-z0-9_]{0,63}$`) — never profiles. REQUIRED, and EMPTY IS MEANINGFUL: an empty list declares that the Snapp handles none, where an absent one declares nothing. Item atom kind and token shape are NOT enforced by this type (list items do not enforce; a `format` facet is not applied); they are left to the block's JSON schema.

ExercisedDomains.description: {ExercisedDomains} Object Block — domain names to the subjects exercised in each, keyed by the domain itself

ExercisedDomain.description: {ExercisedDomain} Object Block — the subjects of one domain a Snapp exercises

subjects.description: The subject tokens (`^[a-z][a-z0-9_]{0,63}$`, the grammar of `Subject.key`) this Snapp exercises in the domain. At least one, no duplicates. Item atom kind is NOT enforced (list items do not enforce); it is left to the block's JSON schema.
